articles.title: New API Documentation
articles.description: Start using AI APIs in a few minutes.

sections.title: What is New API?
sections.body: New API lets your app send a message, create an image or use another supported AI model through one API account. Start with a key, a model and one small request.

sections.title: Three things you need
sections.body:
- **Base URL**: the address your app connects to. Copy the address shown below.
- **API Key**: your private access key, created in [API Keys](/keys).
- **Model ID**: the exact model name. Find it in [Models](/docs/models) and use Copy. Different models support different tasks.

articles.title: Quickstart
articles.description: Your first AI response in five short steps.

sections.title: 1. Sign in
sections.body: [Sign in](/sign-in), or [create an account](/sign-up) if registration is available.

sections.title: 2. Create an API key
sections.body: Open [API Keys](/keys), choose **Create API Key**, then copy the key. Keep it private.

sections.title: 3. Choose a model
sections.body: Open [Models](/docs/models), choose a Text model that supports chat, and copy its Model ID. Your key must have access to that model.

sections.title: 4. Copy and run
sections.body: Set `NEW_API_KEY` and `NEW_API_MODEL` in your terminal. Choose cURL, Python or JavaScript below, copy the example and run it. For Python install `openai`; for JavaScript install `openai`; cURL also needs `jq`.

sections.title: 5. Check the result
sections.body: Your request goes to the model, which returns an answer. Its usage determines the cost. Open [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common) to see the request and its **Cost**. If it fails, use [Common errors](/docs/error-codes).

articles.title: API Key
articles.description: Create, copy and protect your API key.

sections.title: Create and copy
sections.body: Open [API Keys](/keys), choose **Create API Key**, give it a name and save. Open its actions to **Copy Key** or **Copy Connection Info**. Use a separate key for each app when possible.

sections.title: Use your key safely
sections.body: An API key lets an app use your account balance. Put it in your app settings or a server environment variable. Never share it, publish it in code or send it in a screenshot.

sections.title: If a key is exposed
sections.body: Open [API Keys](/keys), **Disable** or **Delete** the exposed key, then create a new one and update your apps. Deleting or disabling a key stops future requests using it.

articles.title: Models
articles.description: Choose a model and copy its ID.

sections.title: Choose by task
sections.body: Use Text for chat, Image for pictures, Video for clips, or Audio for speech. Search by model name or provider. A type is shown only when the platform supplies supporting information.

sections.title: Copy the Model ID
sections.body: Use **Copy** beside a model name. Paste that exact ID into your app or the request example. A listed model still needs permission on your API key; if access fails, check the key settings.

articles.title: Pricing
articles.description: See the price before you send a request.

sections.title: Read the price
sections.body: The prices below come from this platform. Text may have separate input and output prices. Image, video and audio use the unit shown for that model; there is no single unit for every model.

sections.title: Check what you paid
sections.body: Prices can depend on your account and request options. Public prices marked **From** show a starting price. The request's **Cost** in [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common) is the amount recorded for your usage.

articles.title: Text / Chat
articles.description: Send a message and receive an AI answer.

sections.title: What it does
sections.body: Use Text / Chat for questions, writing and supported coding tasks. Choose a model with OpenAI chat support in [Models](/docs/models).

sections.title: Endpoint and response
sections.body: Send `POST /v1/chat/completions`. `model` is your Model ID; `messages` contains your conversation. A normal response has the answer in `choices[0].message.content`. Usage and cost appear in [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common).

sections.title: Common options
sections.body: Start with `model` and `messages`. In **Advanced options**, `stream` delivers the answer in pieces. `temperature` changes randomness and `max_tokens` limits the answer length, where the selected model supports them. Begin without optional fields if the model rejects one.

articles.title: Image
articles.description: Create a picture from a prompt.

sections.title: Prompt and model
sections.body: Describe the picture you want. Choose a model that supports image generation, then send `POST /v1/images/generations` with `model` and `prompt`.

sections.title: Options and result
sections.body: Depending on the model, `size` controls dimensions and `n` controls image count. Start with one image and omit optional settings until you check the model's support. The result can contain an image URL or encoded image data; async providers may return a task.

sections.title: If it takes too long
sections.body: Check [Task Logs](/usage-logs/task) before sending the same request again. An image task can continue after a timeout and still incur a charge when it finishes.

articles.title: Video
articles.description: Create a video and check when it is ready.

sections.title: Create a video
sections.body: Choose a supported video model, write a prompt and send `POST /v1/videos`. The response gives you a task `id`; the video is not usually ready immediately.

sections.title: Check and download
sections.body: Create task → save its ID → check `GET /v1/videos/{task_id}` → when `status` is `completed`, download `GET /v1/videos/{task_id}/content`. If it is `failed`, inspect [Task Logs](/usage-logs/task).

sections.title: Model-specific options
sections.body: Duration, resolution, aspect ratio, reference images and audio options vary by model. Only use options supported by your chosen model; the first example omits them. Check task status before retrying to avoid creating a second paid task.

articles.title: Audio
articles.description: Turn text into speech or speech into text.

sections.title: Text-to-speech
sections.body: Send `POST /v1/audio/speech` with a supported `model`, your text in `input`, and a supported `voice`. A normal response is audio data. Some async models return task JSON instead; check the response type before saving an audio file.

sections.title: Speech-to-text
sections.body: Send `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` with your audio `file` and a supported `model` as multipart form data. The response includes the transcribed `text`.

sections.title: Choose a supported model
sections.body: Speech generation and transcription are different tasks. Check the model's support and price rather than assuming every Audio model can do both.

articles.title: Claude Code
articles.description: Connect Claude Code with your gateway key.

sections.title: Configure
sections.body: Create a dedicated [API key](/keys). Set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to this gateway's origin **without `/v1`**, and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` to that key. Choose a model that supports Anthropic Messages in [Models](/docs/models). Set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to its exact ID, then start Claude Code in the same terminal.

sections.title: Test
sections.body: Send one short prompt, check `/status` in Claude Code and review [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common). Client versions and model features differ; this gateway does not enable the count-tokens endpoint. See the [official Claude Code gateway guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect).

articles.title: Cursor
articles.description: Use your API key in supported Cursor settings.

sections.title: Configure
sections.body: Create a dedicated [API key](/keys). Open Cursor **Settings → Models**. If your version provides **Override OpenAI Base URL**, enter the OpenAI Base URL below, save your key and choose an accessible chat model ID.

sections.title: Test
sections.body: Send a short chat prompt and check [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common). Support depends on Cursor's version and provider controls. Your key does not replace every Cursor feature, including Tab completion, and requests pass through Cursor's servers. See the [official Cursor API key guide](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/api-keys).

sections.title: Configure
sections.body: Create a dedicated [API key](/keys). In Cline settings choose **OpenAI Compatible**. Paste the OpenAI Base URL below, your key and the exact Model ID copied from [Models](/docs/models).

sections.title: Test
sections.body: Send a short prompt and inspect [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common). Only enable image or tool features when the model supports them. See the [official Cline setup guide](https://docs.cline.bot/provider-config/openai-compatible).

articles.title: OpenAI-compatible Apps
articles.description: Connect apps that offer a Custom OpenAI API setting.

sections.title: Three settings
sections.body: Most compatible apps need **Base URL**, **API Key** and **Model ID**. Use the OpenAI Base URL below, a key from [API Keys](/keys) and an accessible chat model copied from [Models](/docs/models). Avoid adding `/v1` twice if the app appends it.

sections.title: Test a small request
sections.body: Send one short message, then open [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common). Basic chat support does not guarantee every app feature. If a setting is missing or the request fails, check the app's own documentation and [Common errors](/docs/error-codes).

articles.title: Balance & Top-up
articles.description: Check your balance and add credit.

sections.title: Your balance
sections.body: Open [Wallet](/wallet) to see **Current Balance** and the payment or redemption options available on this platform. Your balance decreases as requests use paid services.

sections.title: After a payment
sections.body: Check [Payment history](/wallet?show_history=true) to confirm the order status. If credit has not arrived, check that status before paying again and contact support with the order ID. Never share your payment credentials.

articles.title: Usage & Logs
articles.description: See your requests and their actual cost.

sections.title: Check a request
sections.body: Open [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common) and find the request by time or model. The log shows its model, usage and **Cost**; available status and error information helps explain failures.

sections.title: Check a task
sections.body: Use [Task Logs](/usage-logs/task) for video and other async work. Check whether the task is still running, completed or failed before starting it again. The final cost or refund can be recorded after completion.

articles.title: Billing
articles.description: Understand when and how you pay.

sections.title: When am I charged?
sections.body: Successful requests are charged using the model's configured price and recorded usage. Text can charge separately for input and output tokens. Image, video and audio use the unit displayed on [Pricing](/docs/pricing).

sections.title: What if a request fails?
sections.body: Failed requests normally return reserved balance. Completed work or configured policy fees may still be charged. A timed-out task can keep running, so check [Task Logs](/usage-logs/task) before trying again.

sections.title: Where is the exact cost?
sections.body: Open [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common) and read **Cost** for that request. Use [Wallet](/wallet) for your remaining balance. Task charges or refunds can be finalized later; the initial balance change is not always the final cost.

articles.title: FAQ
articles.description: Short answers to the questions people ask first.

sections.title: Where do I get my API key?
sections.body: Open [API Keys](/keys), create a key and use **Copy Key**.

sections.title: What are Base URL and Model ID?
sections.body: Base URL is the server address your app connects to. Model ID is the exact model name you copy from [Models](/docs/models). See [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart).

sections.title: Why is my balance insufficient?
sections.body: Check [Wallet](/wallet) and your key's quota. Add credit if needed, or check your subscription limits. See [Billing](/docs/billing).

sections.title: Why is a model unavailable?
sections.body: Check the model ID, your key's access and the task type. A visible model may be unavailable for your key or temporarily have no working provider. See [Common errors](/docs/error-codes).

sections.title: Which models create images or videos?
sections.body: Use the Image or Video filter on [Models](/docs/models). The type is based on supplied metadata, so unknown types are not guessed.

sections.title: What do 401, 429 or a timeout mean?
sections.body: 401 usually means the key is invalid, expired or disabled. 429 means a request limit was reached. On a timeout, check the request or task status before retrying. See [Common errors](/docs/error-codes).

sections.title: How do I check the cost?
sections.body: Open [Usage Logs](/usage-logs/common), find the request and read **Cost**.

articles.title: Common errors
articles.description: Find the cause and the next step.

sections.title: Read the message
sections.body: Check both the HTTP status and the response message. The same status can have different causes. This gateway uses **403**, not a fixed 402, for insufficient account or key quota.

sections.title: Before retrying
sections.body: Fix invalid settings first. For limits, wait and try a small request. For image or video timeouts, check [Task Logs](/usage-logs/task) before submitting again; a task may still finish and be charged.
